prompt: Let X be the number of unused reservations on a weekend for one randomly selected park facility. The probability distribution is 2 unused reservations: 0.08; 3 unused reservations: 0.22; 4 unused reservations: 0.39; 5 unused reservations: 0.31. Calculate the standard deviation of X.

misconception_source.label: Computed spread from equally weighted values instead of probabilities

sources.note: sigma_X = sqrt(sum (x_i - mu_X)^2 P(x_i)); the probabilities weight each squared deviation

misconception_source.label: Reported the variance instead of the standard deviation

sources.note: standard deviation sigma_X is the square root of V(X); variance and standard deviation are distinct parameters

misconception_source.label: Averaged the possible values without weighting by probability

sources.note: 2025 CR Report Q3/Q5 documents computing the unweighted mean of possible X-values instead of the probability-weighted mean

worked_solution: mu_X = sum x_i P(x_i) = 2(0.08) + 3(0.22) + 4(0.39) + 5(0.31) = 3.9300. Variance = sum (x_i - mu_X)^2 P(x_i) = 0.8451. sigma_X = sqrt(0.8451) = 0.9193 unused reservations.
